newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip on Yeltsin health worries.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip on Yeltsin health worries.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Tuesday as jittery investors mopped their brows over President Boris Yeltsin's health, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 0.12 percent to 186.14 on $27.62 million in volume.
Share prices rose in early trade on robust Western support, but sank in the afternoon on rumours about Yeltsin's low haemoglobin, said Andrei Ippolitov, corporate securities director at IK Prospekt.
"Although the rumours were dispelled, maybe someone decided to take profits and prices slipped," he said.
The head of Yeltsin's press office denied reports that the president was too sick to undergo his planned heart operation because his haemoglobin level was too low.
Sergei Yastrzhembsky said that preparations for the bypass operation was going according to plan.
Creditanstalt Grant trader Andrei Galperin said sales were initiated by panicky Russian traders, but that Western operators held onto their paper.
"The West was and is in a buying mood," he said.
Traders forecast a downward correction in prices tomorrow and a rise on Thursday, mainly in second-tier shares.
Kondpetroleum was traded at $1.42 after $1.35 at Monday's close, GUM rose to $21.2 from $20.2, Lenerergo fell to $0.377 from $0.420 and UES was $0.0840 after $0.0836.
